examples.run: session 1114's evaluation, asked 2026-10-23 through POST /api/ask, the grid's own chat
examples.question: What did a 4-hour battery at CAISO's SP15 hub earn in total on the day-ahead strategy in September 2026, in USD per MW?
examples.answer: A 1 MW, 4-hour battery at CAISO's SP15 hub (TH_SP15_GEN-APND) earned a total of 6321.48 USD/MW in September 2026 on the day-ahead strategy (battery_stack_monthly, derived). Of that, energy was 2441.58 USD/MW and ancillary services were 3879.89 USD/MW (same table). All 30 of the month's 30 days were held, and none were left out (battery_stack_monthly). The month is a Pacific local month, and the figure is USD per MW of battery for the month, not per year. This is a modeled figure from one linear program a day. The battery is a price taker, and reserves are assumed to be paid and never called. It is not an actual fleet's earnings and includes no capacity payment.

examples.answer: NYISO's N.Y.C. zone had a day-ahead load-weighted price of 105.98 USD/MWh for February 2025 (cost_of_power_monthly, derived). examples.question: What was the average real-time shape premium at NYISO's N.Y.C. zone over the twelve months of 2025?
examples.answer: The mean of the twelve monthly real-time shape premiums at NYISO N.Y.C. for January to December 2025 is 4.36 USD/MWh (cost_of_power_monthly, variable rt_shape_premium, derived table, an unweighted mean of 12 monthly values). Monthly values range from 0.99 USD/MWh (May) to 19.74 USD/MWh (June). Treat the figure with caution, because no month is complete. Real-time hours held total 8256 against 8760 hours in the year (cost_of_power_monthly). For example, February has 600 of 672 hours, and July has 648 of 744. Months are local operating months. The table is derived and public. The shape premium is the load-weighted price minus the simple-mean price.
